fred-us-cpi-2026-08-12.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of consumer prices in the United States. It is the most watched read on US inflation, and it moves rate expectations, bond yields and the dollar.
fred-us-cpi-2026-08-12.recent: The Fed held rates at 350-375 basis points on July 29, citing 'elevated' inflation, after facing growing pressure to hike as price risks rebound. The dollar has since fallen to its weakest since May with a rate hike in doubt. This is the next inflation reading the committee sees before it meets again.

fred-us-ppi-2026-08-13.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly producer price index, which measures what US producers receive for their output. It leads consumer inflation, and its services components feed directly into the Federal Reserve's preferred price gauge.
fred-us-ppi-2026-08-13.recent: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reports US PPI on 13 August, setting the first reading of producer-side inflation that markets will weigh against the consumer figures.

fred-us-retail-sales-2026-08-14.standing: The Census Bureau's monthly report on receipts at US retail and food-service businesses, released mid-month for the month before. It is the earliest broad read on consumer spending, which drives most of the US economy, and it moves rate expectations and the dollar.
fred-us-retail-sales-2026-08-14.recent: The Census Bureau reports US retail sales on 14 August. The release will settle how much of the quarter's consumer spending held up.

ecb-2026-09.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council sets interest rates for the euro area, meeting roughly every six weeks. Its decisions set borrowing costs across twenty member economies and move the euro against every currency it trades with.
ecb-2026-09.recent: The decision follows a run of holds at peers: the Bank of England kept rates at 3.75% with three of nine policymakers voting to raise, the Bank of Japan held at 1% while warning underlying inflation exceeds its 2% target, and the Fed held citing elevated inflation. The dollar has since fallen to its lowest level since May.

fomc-2026-09.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the target range for overnight bank lending. Its decisions move the cost of borrowing across the dollar economy and every asset priced against it.
fomc-2026-09.recent: The Fed held at 350-375 basis points in July, citing elevated inflation, after investors had priced a hike. Since then the dollar has fallen to its weakest since May, and Trump has renewed his bid to remove Cook, reviving the fight over Fed independence. This meeting settles whether the fuel-led inflation of the summer changes the rate.

boe-2026-09.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who meet eight times a year to set Bank Rate. Its votes set the cost of borrowing across the UK economy, feeding through to mortgages, house prices and sterling.
boe-2026-09.recent: The committee held at 3.75% on 30 July with three of nine voting to raise, a split driven by the supply shock from the Iran war. UK house prices rose 0.1% in July as buyers stayed cautious on rates. This meeting settles whether the dissenting minority becomes a majority.

boj-2026-09.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board meets eight times a year to set the short-term policy rate. Its decisions set the price of the world's cheapest major funding currency, and move the yen, Japanese government bonds, and global carry trades.

uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The Office for National Statistics' monthly measure of UK consumer prices, released mid-month for the preceding month. It sets the reference point for Bank of England rate decisions, index-linked gilts, and a range of benefits and contracts uprated by inflation.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: The Office for National Statistics reports September consumer price inflation on 21 October. The release will settle where UK price growth stands going into the Bank of England's autumn decisions.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The rate-setting committee of the US Federal Reserve, which meets eight times a year to set the target range for overnight bank lending. Its decisions set the price of dollar credit worldwide, moving currencies, sovereign borrowing costs and every asset priced in dollars.
fomc-2026-10.recent: The Fed held at 350-375 basis points in July, citing elevated inflation, after investors had priced a hike and Citadel bet on one. Since then the dollar has fallen to its weakest since May with a hike in doubt, and Trump has moved again to fire Cook, reviving the fight over Fed independence.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which sets interest rates for the euro area on a schedule of eight meetings a year. Its decisions set borrowing costs across twenty member economies and transmit through the euro to trade and debt priced against it.
ecb-2026-10.recent: The decision falls in a stretch where major central banks have split on what inflation demands. The Bank of England held at 3.75% with three of nine policymakers voting to raise, the Bank of Japan held at 1% while warning underlying inflation exceeds its 2% target, and the Fed held citing elevated inflation.

boj-2026-10.standing: Japan's central bank sets short-term policy rates and buys government bonds, meeting eight times a year. Because Japan is the world's largest creditor nation, its rate decisions move global bond yields and the borrowing costs of carry trades funded in yen.
boj-2026-10.recent: The Bank of Japan held rates at 1% on July 31 while warning of underlying inflation exceeding its 2% target, and Tokyo sold dollars for yen hours before the decision. Japan then confirmed a historic joint yen intervention with the US, which pushed the dollar to a one-month low. This meeting will settle whether the rate stays behind the currency defence.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote individually on Bank Rate at eight scheduled meetings a year. Bank Rate sets the floor for UK mortgage, business and government borrowing costs, and moves sterling.
boe-2026-11.recent: The committee held at 3.75% on 30 July, waiting to see the impact of the Iran war, with three of nine voting to raise. That split leaves the November meeting to settle whether the supply shock has fed far enough into UK prices to force a move, against a housing market where prices rose 0.1% in July.
